title: Hiibel v. Sixth Judicial District Court (2004)
citation: Hiibel v. Sixth Judicial Dist. Court of Nev., 542 U.S. 177 (2004)
key_points: Holding: A state law requiring a person lawfully stopped on reasonable suspicion to state their name did not violate the Fourth or Fifth Amendment.
officer_notes: Scenario: During a valid Terry stop you ask for the person's name and they refuse.
Takeaway: Whether refusal to give a name is itself an offense depends on state law; check NJ law and your prosecutor's guidance before charging.
